title: Control-ITRA: Controlling the Behavior of a Driving Model

control_signal.value: Per-agent waypoints to follow and a per-agent target speed (used as an indirect aggressiveness knob); conditioning can be partial, on either or both.

control_mechanism.value: Waypoints are placed on the ego-centric birdview input; target speed enters through conditional affine transforms (scale and shift) of layer features. Training conditions are sampled from ground-truth trajectories; unconditional use is supported.

base_model.value: ITRA: rasterized birdview multi-agent driving model, each agent a variational recurrent network.

datasets.value: Training on a drone-recorded dataset of more than 1000 hours from 19 countries (4-second segments, 10Hz); out-of-domain tests in TorchDriveEnv.

metrics.value: Realism: ADE, FDE, minADE/minFDE over 6 samples, miss rate; diversity: MFD; safety: collision, offroad, traffic-light violation rates; condition-reaching rate; TorchDriveEnv return and waypoints reached.

controllability_evidence.value: TorchDriveEnv single-agent: Control-ITRA with waypoints reaches 4.54 waypoints (return 533.02, collision rate 0.0) vs 2.06 waypoints (return 297.98) unconditionally; it also beats SAC, PPO, TD3, A2C baselines.

stated_limitations.value: No explicit limitations in packet; future work proposes more abstract controls such as natural language commands or driver intentions. Training with last-timestep conditions degrades on 8-second rollouts.

notes: Table cell alignment in the packet is garbled; numbers taken from Table 3 rows as read. Target-speed controllability numbers (Tables 1-2) are not legible in the packet.
